\section[l'esplosione]{l'esplosione — the explosion}

\label{lesson:IT-C303-esplosione}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the burn, then the Italian for to get burned.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: l'esplosione}
\textbf{l'esplosione} — \textquotedblleft{}the explosion\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
L'esplosione si è sentita in tutto il paese.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The explosion was heard all over the village.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Un'esplosione di gas} — a gas explosion.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{esplosione} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{explōsiō} (EtymDB), from \emph{explōdere} \textquotedblleft{}to drive off by clapping\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{l'esplosione}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{l'esplosione}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{l'esplosione}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the burn, then the Italian for to get burned, then say \emph{l'esplosione} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does l'esplosione mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The explosion\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[esplodere]{esplodere — to explode, to blow up}

\label{lesson:IT-C303-esplodere}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for to get burned, then the Italian for the explosion.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: esplodere}
\textbf{esplodere} — \textquotedblleft{}to explode, to blow up\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Una bombola di gas è esplosa.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{A gas cylinder exploded.}
\end{quote}

With \emph{essere}: \emph{è esploso}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{esplodere} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{explōdere} \textquotedblleft{}to drive off with clapping\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), from \emph{ex} and \emph{plaudere} \textquotedblleft{}to clap\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{esplodere}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{esplodere}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{esplodere}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for to get burned, then the Italian for the explosion, then say \emph{esplodere} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does esplodere mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To explode, to blow up\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[scoppiare]{scoppiare — to burst; to break out}

\label{lesson:IT-C303-scoppiare}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the explosion, then the Italian for to explode.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: scoppiare}
\textbf{scoppiare} — \textquotedblleft{}to burst; to break out\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
È scoppiata una gomma.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{A tyre burst.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Scoppiare a ridere} — to burst out laughing; \emph{è scoppiata la guerra} — war broke out.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{scoppiare} is built on \emph{scoppio} \textquotedblleft{}a bang\textquotedblright{}, from Late Latin \emph{scloppus} \textquotedblleft{}a slapping sound\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{scoppiare}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{scoppiare}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{scoppiare}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the explosion, then the Italian for to explode, then say \emph{scoppiare} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does scoppiare mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To burst; to break out\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[lo scoppio]{lo scoppio — the bang, the burst; the outbreak}

\label{lesson:IT-C303-scoppio}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for to explode, then the Italian for to burst.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: lo scoppio}
\textbf{lo scoppio} — \textquotedblleft{}the bang, the burst; the outbreak\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Abbiamo sentito uno scoppio fortissimo.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We heard a very loud bang.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Lo scoppio della guerra} — the outbreak of war.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{scoppio} goes back to Late Latin \emph{scloppus} \textquotedblleft{}a slapping sound\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), a word that imitates the sound.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[il crollo]{il crollo — the collapse}

\label{lesson:IT-C303-crollo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for to burst, then the Italian for the bang.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: il crollo}
\textbf{il crollo} — \textquotedblleft{}the collapse\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Il crollo del ponte ha bloccato la città.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The collapse of the bridge brought the city to a halt.}
\end{quote}

Also for prices: \emph{il crollo della borsa}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{crollo} is built on \emph{crollare} \textquotedblleft{}to collapse\textquotedblright{}, which is usually traced to a Vulgar Latin \emph{corrotulāre} \textquotedblleft{}to roll down\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short gives \emph{rotula} \textquotedblleft{}a small wheel\textquotedblright{}).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for to burst, then the Italian for the bang, then say \emph{il crollo} again
